title: Model Adoption Early-Warning System: signals, scoring, and playbooks
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Build an early-warning system that surfaces changes in the external model landscape and internal adoption signals that could materially affect Redwood product positioning, product/engineering priorities, and commercial motion. The system should combine public signals (model launches, license/price changes, technical capabilities), partner/market signals (marketplace listings, cloud integrations), and customer telemetry (usage shifts, support tickets, eval failures) into a prioritized score and trigger playbooks for PM/SE/marketing.
background: We routinely react to model releases or pricing moves after customer inquiries. That reactive posture increases churn risk and slows product decisions. A lightweight but actionable EWS will reduce time-to-response and help prioritize compatibility, runtime optimizations, and marketing countermeasures.
mvp_scope: Phase 1 (6 weeks): ingest 3 signal types (public model release RSS + GitHub tags, cloud marketplace listings, top-customer usage delta). Build a scoring function (0-100), dashboard with top-10 active signals, and two playbooks (investigate vs. urgent escalations). Alerting to PM on score > 70 and weekly digest to GTM.
signal_spec: Public releases: model name, version, license, quantization availability, release notes link, date
Open-source activity: GitHub stars/forks delta and new language/ops integrations
Pricing/licensing changes: new commercial licenses, free tiers, or vendor discounts
Marketplace/partner releases: cloud provider model listings and managed endpoints
Customer telemetry: top 20 customers' model-selection shifts and latency/cost anomalies
Support & sales signals: frequency of feature requests referencing competitor model features or performance
scoring_rubric: Weighted multi-signal model. Initial weights: customer_telemetry:40, public_release:25, pricing:15, marketplace:10, support:10. Score normalization by recency and population affected. Manual override flags for legal/licensing risk. Thresholds: 0-39 low, 40-69 medium, 70+ high.
playbooks: Investigate (score 40-69): assign product analyst + research brief, run bench through Redwood quick-eval harness, draft PRD impact note
Urgent (score 70+): notify execs, open dedicated war-room Slack channel, schedule runtime/eng triage for compatibility and fallback strategy, prepare GTM comms
Customer-impact mitigation: for affected customers, create targeted outreach template and temporary routing to alternate model variants
success_metrics: Mean time from signal detection to first triage action < 72 hours
Reduction in reactive product tickets referencing competitor releases by 60% over 3 months
Fraction of high-severity signals with a documented mitigation plan within 7 days > 90%
data_requirements: Public feeds: RSS/Atom + API polling for model hub(s) and GitHub (requires token)
Customer telemetry: model use events, route-level token counts, latency and cost metrics (requires instrumentation and consent for enterprise customers)
Support/Sales: aggregated taggable signal from Zendesk/Intercom and Salesforce
tradeoffs_and_risks: False positives: noisy public signals could waste engineering cycles; mitigate with higher customer-telemetry weight
Data privacy: avoid storing identifiable customer data in public EWS; use aggregated deltas and hashed IDs
Maintenance cost: keeping scrapers and parsers up-to-date across many model hubs requires upkeep—start with 3 highest-value sources
Alert fatigue: conservative thresholds for human alerts, use weekly digest to reduce noise
deliverables: Signal ingestion pipeline (3 sources) + data schema doc
Scoring microservice and mapping table for weights
EWS dashboard in Looker/Grafana with drill-down links
Two operational playbooks + alerting rules in PagerDuty/Slack
Handbook page (Confluence) describing run-rate and escalation paths
initial_timeline: Week 0-1: source selection and data access. Week 2-3: ingestion + normalization. Week 4: scoring function + unit tests. Week 5: dashboard + alerting. Week 6: dry-run with synthetic signals and stakeholder review.
